blocks.en: If $f$ is in $C^1(\Omega)$, this definition agrees with the classical derivative, as can be seen by an integration by parts. It is easy to see that $\partial f/\partial x_j$ is again in $\mathcal{D}^{\prime}(\Omega)$.
blocks.zh: 若 $f$ 属于 $C^1(\Omega)$, 则这一定义与经典导数一致, 通过分部积分即可看出. 容易看出, $\partial f/\partial x_j$ 仍属于 $\mathcal{D}^{\prime}(\Omega)$.

blocks.en: If $f_n\to f$ in $\mathcal{D}^{\prime}(\Omega)$ then $\partial f_n/\partial x_j\to\partial f/\partial x_j$.
blocks.zh: 若在 $\mathcal{D}^{\prime}(\Omega)$ 中 $f_n\to f$, 则 $\partial f_n/\partial x_j\to\partial f/\partial x_j$.
blocks.label: thm:distribution-derivative-continuity

blocks.en: Thus, for distributions exchanging derivatives and limits is no problem, quite a contrast to the situation in classical calculus.
blocks.zh: 因此, 对分布而言, 交换导数与极限没有问题, 这与经典微积分中的情况形成鲜明对比.
